data.name: Narad
data.gender_notes: Narad is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Narada is a sage and celestial musician mentioned in Hindu mythology. He travels between the gods and humans, acting as a messenger and narrator of tales. The name Narad carries the meaning “Man of the people” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Narad usually hope their child will grow to embody man of the people and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Carrier of divine knowledge and wisdom.
data.etymology: Narad belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Man of the people.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Narad total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: Narada is a revered figure in Hindu mythology, often portrayed as a wise and knowledgeable sage who acts as a bridge between gods and humans. He is known for his musical skills and is said to be able to charm even the most stubborn beings with his melodies. Narada is also a significant character in many Hindu scriptures and Puranas, and his stories and teachings continue to be an important part of Hindu culture and traditions, especially in the form of Indian music and art.
data.spiritual_significance: Narada is considered a representation of the divine consciousness that pervades the universe, with the ability to traverse both the material and spiritual realms. He embodies the qualities of wisdom, compassion, and detachment, inspiring us to look beyond the physical world and seek the deeper truths of existence. By following the teachings and stories of Narada, we can deepen our spiritual understanding and develop a stronger connection with the divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Narad is the celestial sage and messenger of the gods, symbolizing wisdom, interconnectedness, and the power of speech. He brings knowledge and truth to those in need, fostering growth and understanding.

historical_references.reference: Narada is mentioned in the Hindu epic Mahabharata, where he acts as a messenger between the gods and the demons, and also between various gods and sages. He is known for his wisdom, knowledge of music, and his ability to create illusions.

Narada is also mentioned in the Puranas, a collection of 18 Hindu texts that preserve ancient Indian traditions and mythology. He is described as the creator of the universe, who travelled throughout the cosmos singing the praises of the gods and spreading their stories.

modern_usage.modern_context: Narad Muni, also known as Narada, is a significant character in Hindu mythology, often depicted as a wandering sage and the creator of the universe's illusion. In modern contexts, Narad's storytelling abilities have been explored across various platforms. He is a popular character in webseries, such as 'Narad Muni: The Wanderer,' where he is portrayed as a charismatic and enlightened sage. In animation, Narad is featured in shows like 'Mahabharata' and 'Ramayana,' where his role as a messenger of the gods and a creator of cosmic illusions is brought to life through vibrant visuals. Lastly, in the realm of audio books, listeners can enjoy stories of Narad's adventures and wisdom through recordings that bring the ancient tales to life in a modern and accessible way.
